supporting_quotes: In this article, we develop novel preference learning models for multimodal emotion recognition that address the mismatch between the perceived labels on different modalities, as well as the mismatch between the intended and perceived emotions in each modality.

In contrast to previous studies that relied on either the intended or the perceived emotion labels, we argue that both intended and perceived labels contain valuable information about how humans express and perceive emotions, which should be collectively mined to improve the accuracy of emotion recognition.
criterion_assessments.notes: The work presents original models and evaluations; it is not a survey or review.

supporting_quotes: Numerous studies have demonstrated that humans excel at comparing two options rather than assigning absolute labels [4–6]. Thus, a growing body of work has recognised their importance and adopted ordinal regression or preference learning frameworks for emotion recognition [7–10].

Approaches to converting interval labels to ROLs typically involve pairwise comparisons between all pairs of interval labels at different times and retain information about the relationship (greater/lesser) and discarding details of interval label values [9, 16, 17].
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text explicitly discusses preference learning in emotion recognition and references pairwise comparisons as a core mechanism, indicating an in-scope preference-learning path.

supporting_quotes: The MSP-Podcast corpus is a large naturalistic speech emotional dataset that is collected from real-life podcast recordings [13].

To validate the converted AOLs, we compare it with both the original interval labels as well as categorical labels obtained independently to describe the same data.
criterion_assessments.notes: The work explicitly uses speech/emotion corpora (audio domain) for validation and experiments.

supporting_quotes: Retrieving speech samples that have specific expressive content has many applications.
It is desirable to build a preference learning framework that ranks speech samples according to emotional attribute values that generalize well to new domains.
A popular architecture for preference learning is the RankNet framework, which uses a function to obtain the preference between pairs of speech sentences.
This study implements RankNet using state-of-the-art domain adaptation strategies to increase the generalization of the models when evaluated on a different domain.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text directly supports the preference-learning path.

supporting_quotes: we implement our preference-learning based speech emotion recognition (SER) system using ladder networks and adversarial domain adaptation.
ranks speech samples according to emotional attribute values
The MSP-Podcast corpus [31] as the source domain. We use release 1.10 consisting of 104,267 speaking turns from different audio recordings with Creative Commons licenses.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text clearly situates the work in audio (speech emotion recognition) and evaluates with audio datasets.

supporting_quotes: This study explores two unsupervised approaches that have been successfully implemented on SER: ladder network [22], using intermediate layer representation reconstructions, and adversarial domain adaptation (DA) [23], using domain classification implemented with a gradient reversal.
This is the first attempt to make a preference learning-based SER model robust to different domains.
criterion_assessments.notes: The article presents original methodology and experimental results rather than a survey or review.

supporting_quotes: The RankNet algorithm was introduced by Burges [20].
The function f(·) is trained using the ground truth labels with preferences between sample pairs.

The cost function L = −¯Pij log Pij − (1 −¯Pij) log(1 −Pij) is the cross entropy between the expected probability ¯Pij and actual probability Pij, which is used to train the parameters of the function f(·).
criterion_assessments.notes: The paper describes learning/training of RankNet, not evaluation-only usage of preferences.

supporting_quotes: An important task in human-computer interaction is to rank speech samples according to their expressive content.

criterion_assessments.notes: Audio-domain application as described (speech samples with emotion attributes).

supporting_quotes: The experiments show that the use of the proposed anchor-based ordinal labels leads to significantly better performance than models trained using existing alternative labels.

criterion_assessments.notes: Not a survey or review; presents an experimental method and results.

supporting_quotes: Current emotional TTS models pre-dominantly conduct supervised training to learn the conversion from text and desired emotion to its emotional speech, focusing on a single emotion per text-speech pair.

criterion_assessments.notes: The text is clearly in the audio domain (emotional TTS) and discusses audio outputs.

supporting_quotes: Beyond Single Emotions: we propose Emo-DPO, a novel controllable emotional TTS approach that leverages direct preference optimization to differentiate subtle differences between emotions for the first time
This paper presents a controllable emotional TTS approach with the integration of emotion-aware TTS-LLM architecture, opening doors for advancing emotional speech synthesis in the era of LLMs.
criterion_assessments.notes: These indicate a primary research contribution rather than a survey/review.

supporting_quotes: Motivation: Yet, simply conducting instruction tuning on π may be insufficient, as the model only learns to generate the correct output without fully understanding why it is correct. To equip the model with the ability to capture subtle differences between the desired emotional speech and other emotions with the same semantic content, we turn to preference learning to further refine its performance.
The DPO objective essentially maximizes the likelihood of π generating y+ while minimizing the likelihood of generating y− conditioned on xj and the emotion trigger word E.
criterion_assessments.notes: The work uses preference learning for model training, not evaluation-only use.

Burges et al. [18] introduced RankNet, an algorithm that uses gradient descent to perform preference learning between pairs of samples.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text explicitly describes a preference-learning approach based on pairwise ranking using RankNet (a deep learning ranker) applied to emotional attributes in speech.

This study relies on two emotional databases with conversational speech.

criterion_assessments.notes: The entire study is applied to speech audio data and acoustic features, supporting full in-domain audio application.

supporting_quotes: A popular architecture for preference learning is the RankNet framework, which uses a function to obtain the preference between pairs of speech sentences.
We consider the chunk-based segmentation (CBS) proposed by Lin and Busso [27,28] to obtain a fixed dimensional discriminative feature vector for variable-length speech segments.
The RankNet algorithm uses a probabilistic cost function to learn preference between pairs of data points using gradient descent.
The function f(·) is trained using the ground truth labels with preferences between sample pairs.
The preference learning framework leads to better precision for retrieval tasks than comparable SER systems built to directly predict absolute emotional attribute scores.

We rely on the qualitative agreement (QA)-based method proposed by Parthasarathy and Busso [19] for obtaining preference labels. The approach identifies trends across individual annotations, instead of relying on the consensus label.

The results demonstrate that building the RankNet function with these training strategies leads to better performance in cross-corpus evaluations than models that are not adapted to the target domain.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text explicitly describes pairwise preference learning using a RankNet framework applying preference comparisons between pairs of speech samples for emotion recognition. It includes detailed methodology and experiments supporting a preference learning approach, satisfying the criterion.

supporting_quotes: we propose a reinforcement learning approach to enhance model robustness, speaker similarity, and controllability.

Specifically, we use REINFORCE to fine-tune two versions based on the original zero-shot ICL model (Seed-TTSICL) using different reward functions: Seed-TTSRL-SIM-WER, which uses the SIM and WER objective metrics as rewards to improve speaker similarity and robustness, and Seed-TTSRL-SER, which uses the accuracy of the SER model as a reward to improve emotion controllability.
We adopt the word error rate (WER) and speaker similarity (SIM) metrics for objective evaluation.
Seed-TTS achieves performance closely matching real human speech for both English and Mandarin with CMOS scores of -0.07 and -0.08, respectively.
criterion_assessments.notes: Full text explicitly describes a preference-learning path based on reinforcement learning applied to the TTS model using reward signals related to speaker similarity and emotion controllability, which qualifies as an in-scope RL training loop for an audio model.

supporting_quotes: We introduce Seed-TTS, a family of large-scale autoregressive text-to-speech (TTS) models capable of generating speech that is virtually indistinguishable from human speech.
Seed-TTS serves as a foundation model for speech generation and excels in speech in-context learning, achieving performance in speaker similarity and naturalness.
We present a non-autoregressive (NAR) variant of the Seed-TTS model, named Seed-TTSDiT, which utilizes a fully diffusion-based architecture.
We demonstrate that this variant achieves comparable performance to the language model-based variant and showcase its effectiveness in speech editing.

Serving as a foundation model for speech generation, Seed-TTS can perform various tasks, such as speech ICL, controllable TTS, cross-lingual TTS, voice conversion, timbre generation, and speaking style transfer.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text clearly situates the work in the audio domain including multiple speech and sound generation and manipulation tasks.

the finetuning objective leverages both a novel reward model that provides feedback on both harmonic and temporal coherency between melody and chord

We develop a novel ensemble of reward models that evaluates the coherence between input (melody) and output (chord) tracks.

We further develop a novel approach that predicts human quality ratings using a pyramid bidirectional long short term memory (pBLSTM) network with an attention mechanism.
